To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the business cycles in a small-open economy can be caused by exogenous periodic perturbation of any parameter.
the economy can experience a business cycle even if there is only one household in the economy.
business cycles appear in a dynamic general-equilibrium framework with heterogeneous households, progressive income taxation, and public goods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.
the effects of progressive income taxation on the business cycles in a small-open economy.
the dynamic effects of progressive income taxation and the dynamic interactions among the economic agents in an economy that is subject to exogenous shocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is capable of generating realistic business cycles with progressive income taxation.
progressive taxation is an efficient and powerful tool for the government to smooth out business cycles and reduce fluctuations of economic variables.
the economic system is robust to exogenous periodic shocks and the economic growth rate is not sensitive to exogenous periodic perturbation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
business cycles are endogenous in a small-open economy.
business cycles are the results of the interactions between the exogenous perturbations and the endogenous wealth accumulation in the model economy.
business cycles are not caused by the exogenous perturbation itself, but rather the interaction between the exogenous perturbations and the economic system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
progressive taxation can be an effective policy tool for stabilizing the economy.
the business cycle is not only a feature of the capitalist economy but also a feature of the socialist economy with progressive income taxation.
progressive income taxation can be an effective policy instrument for stabilizing business cycles.
